MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 28, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:04 p.m., on September 28, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on September 23, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:03 p.m. with five City Council Members present

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

City Council Minutes  1  September 28, 2021
   Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to the "Marines of the Quarter"
  Corporal Jens Peaslee, Corporal Stephani Navarro and Lance Corporal Sara Snaidauf, and
  "Noncommissioned Officers of the Quarter" Corporal Jared Jett, Sergeant Payson Brooks, and
  Staff Sergeant Michael Kerr.

P2. Proclaim October 3 through 9, 2021 To Be "Fire Prevention Week"

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamation to Fire Chief Rob Capobianco.

P3. Santa Margarita Water District- 2021 Drought Update

  Received presentation from Director of External Affairs Jim Leach.

P4. Moulton Niguel Water District - Resilient Together - Partnerships Make Every Drop
  Count

  Received presentation from Assistant General Manager Matt Collings.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Expressed that the mixed-use development proposal for the Old Miners
Village/Garden Plaza is a shell game to move high-density housing instead of the Village Center.

Greg Nelson, M.V.: Commented that the Neighbor Awareness Form that the City requires when
residents want to make exterior improvements is kept in mind at a future meeting when the Council
discusses the Oso Creek Golf Course and Public Space Vision Plan.

Gabirel El-Mahrek, M.V.: Expressed his concerns of LGBTQ+ in mainstream media and asked that
the City ban Gay Pride Month.

Brianna Jokerst, M.V.: Voiced her concerns regarding the Oso Creek Golf Course and Public Space
Vision Plan. Asked that the Council consider the impact of adding additional facilities will have
on the surrounding neighborhoods.

Craig Innis, Rancho Santa Margarita: Stated that he was impressed with the Oso Creek upgrades
and trail extensions, but voiced concerns that the project looked like a theme park.

Cathy Kadison, M.V.: Stressed that the City needs to begin the district mapping process as soon as
the census data is released on September 30. Pointed out that other cities are already holding public
hearings on re-districting. Stated that the delay has cost taxpayers hundreds of thousand of dollars
in legal fees.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Reread her council comments from the last meeting and cited two
denouncement letters from former Secretary of State Alex Padilla regarding the city seeking
cumulative voting, a denouncement letter from the Public Law Library criticizing the City Attorney,
and the letter addressed to the Supreme Court from the City Attorney. She addressed the city
attorney that is a serial liar.

City Council Minutes  2  September 28, 2021
 City Attorney Bill Curley responded to Ms. Schlicht’s comments stating that she is a serial liar,
takes things out of context, and she misrepresents. He expressed that she has a bitter vendetta
against staff and the Council since she had not been re-elected in the previous elections.

Mayor Kelley announced that the YMCA issue is on the agenda later this evening and that the
Council has not been presented with that vision plan. She asked that Mr. Curley respond to Mr.
Gilbert’s and Cathy Kadison’s comments. City Attorney Curley, stated that the Planning
Commission puts out a long-range pending action report. Mr. Gilbert’s comments that the proposed
project at the Miners Village/Garden Plaza was on the action agenda is misinformation. This was
not an action item. A private entity bought this property and they have decided to ask the city for
approval which will be handled in the future in the ordinary course of business, full due process
and full hearing for both sides. This is a standard process where a property owner asks to change
the use of the land. He stated if anyone has questions on what this property owner plans for this
site, they should contact them directly. Regarding Ms. Kadison’s comments on district elections,
Mr. Curley stated that the County is using the same demographer CDR as the City. Due to re-
districting and districting throughout the State, we are queued up with CDR behind the County. We
are not playing games, the courts agreed that our municipal law on four-year terms is in place and
that the two-year terms were set in the event cumulative voting came to be. The standard municipal
code process continues unchanged and the City is following the law.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
remainder of the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 14, 20201, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 27, 2021 in the Amount of $1,473,144.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 3, 2021 in the Amount of $533,491.22

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated September 10, 2021 in the Amount of $3,437,521.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  3  September 28, 2021
 5.  Integrated Library System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $76,318.83 for 1-year maintenance
  and support of the Integrated Library Systems (ILS) Software and Hardware Agreement with
  SirsiDynix, Inc.

6.  Agreement with DynTek Services Inc. for Office 365 Migration Services

  Approved agreement with DynTek Services, Inc. (A21-50) and issued purchase order in an
  amount not to exceed $57,950 for Office 365 migration services.

7.  Tyler Munis ERP Financial, HR, and Payroll Software Renewal

  Approved purchase order to Tyler Technologies, Inc. for 1-year renewal of software licensing
  and support for Munis ERP Financial, Human Resources, and Payroll system in the amount
  of $69,875.34.

8.  Barcelona Wall - Intersection of Alicia Parkway and Charlinda Drive (CIP 330) - Notice
  of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days, respectively, after the
  date of the Notice of Completion recordation and contingent upon the absence of claims or
  liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of
  $3,837.50, thirty-five (35) days after the date of the Notice of Completion recordation.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation - CIP 328

  Motion made by Council member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to
  bifurcate the approval of playground equipment and shade structure to the park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Goodell
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Member Kelley to reject all
  bids and authorized staff to re-bid the project (CIP 328).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodman, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
City Council Minutes  4  September 28, 2021
   Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  the issuance of Purchase Orders for the purchase and delivery of play equipment to the
  following vendors in the related not-to-exceed amounts to Dave Bang Associates, Inc.,
  $68,428.33; and Game Time C/O Great Western Recreation, $45,001.03.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES: Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES: None
  ABENT: None

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell to keep the shade
  covers included in the Coronado Park play area.

  Motion made Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to amend the
  motion on the shade covers to table this item until further review of the trees at the park and
  bring back at the next meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES: Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES: None
  ABENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

10. Legislative Update

  Vice President Cori Takkinen of Townsend Public Affairs gave the legislative update.

  By consensus the City Council received the report.

11. Request by the Tres Vistas Homeowners Association to Manage Pest Control by All
  Authorized means, Including Firearms

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve the request of Tres Vistas Homeowners Association for a variance that will allow the
  association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the
  health, safety and welfare of the community.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS
City Council Minutes  5  September 28, 2021
 12. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented the report.

13. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented the report.

14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Council Member Raths presented the report.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

16.  Update on the YMCA

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the report. He clarified that the City has no plans to
  tear down the YMCA.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Pointed out certain aspects of the Oso Creek Golf Course and Public
  Space Vision Plan and raised concerns about no mention of any new location in the City for
  the YMCA. He feels the Council is not considering the impact of families. Emphasized that
  he did not use the term “tearing down” on his social media but that in the vision plan it states
  that YMCA to be replaced by new Natatorium.

  City Manager Wilberg clarified that he never said that Mr. Gilbert was the one using the term
  “tearing down”. He noted that when the City entered into the agreement with the YMCA that
  Larry was one of a few that opposed this agreement at this location.

  Greg Nelson, M.V: He said he has never seen any proposal or rumor about the consultant or
  the city saying there is a plan to sell the property. He pleads guilty to using the term “tear
  down” of the YMCA based on the wording in the Vision plan that the Natatorium would
  replace the YMCA. He states that he did jump to that conclusion.

  Brianna Jokerst, M.V.: She felt that a lot has been clarified this evening, but did want to point
  out that she can the YMCA from her kitchen window and she did have concerns. She asked
  that down the road if this property is redeveloped that the City considers any environmental
  implications and what the residents want and how it will impact property values.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Addressed Mayor Kelley regarding the relocation of the YMCA in her
  communications with the public and quoted her. Outlined and pointed out different aspects
  of the Vision Plan and asked why the consultant have a vision plan for the YMCA. She also
  criticized the Council on the purchase of the Stein Mart property. Criticized the City Attorney

City Council Minutes  6  September 28, 2021
   that the process he created was crafted for a desired outcome which was to protect to the
  Council Member seats.

  City Attorney Curley responded to Ms. Schlicht that her delusion is right before us, you can
  believe what you want but your bitterness has normalized fiction.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that this is the kind of testimony that generates the
  misinformation. Ms. Schlicht quoted from a number of pages but jumped over page 37 which
  states: “ below is a list of additional ideas and opportunities that the City may consider in the
  long term. Each will require additional analysis to study impacts to adjacent residential
  neighborhoods. He clarified that he tried to explain that it is a good thing for the City that the
  YMCA is interested in expanding their programs. But because of the site limitations, the
  prospect of the YMCA needing to relocate to a larger facility elsewhere withinnnn the city is
  a possibility. He stated that rather than wait for that to happen and then have to decide what
  to do, the city asked the consultant for a list of ideas in the event this should happens as
  indicated on page 37.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Stated that the information that has been shared gave her clarification
  about the YMCA. She reminded the city that budgets are statements of values and
  maintaining the quality of life in Mission Viejo by having a great library, Kids’ Factory, and
  animal services which are services she values. Stated that she appreciates the work the
  Council does although she may not always agree.

  By consensus the City Council received the report.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

Thanked the Councils swift leadership in the YMCA issue particularly the Mayor being
instrumental in setting the facts into motion which is what is important to the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell stated that he attended the recent Lake Association Board Meeting for a
presentation on the status on the water quality of the lake pertaining to golden algae. The Board
is taking steps to remedy this situation. Encouraged residents to get involved.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths attended the Newhart Middle School Steam Building Dedication.

City Council Minutes  7  September 28, 2021
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs thanked the Mayor for responding to all the email regarding the YMCA.
He pointed out that since July 13 this Council has approved $1.9 million in IT software and upgrades
and stressed that the City has already attained half of the $4 million budget. Council Member Sachs
mentioned that according to a CNBC report that there were 25 million new people playing golf this
past year and outlined statistics. He asked that the city staff look into a program at the Osos Creek
Golf Course where residents can bring old golf clubs to donate. Lastly, he asked the City Manager
to take down the plexi-glass on dais.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley attended The Chamber of Commerce State of the City Round Table on September
20 where she had an opportunity to give an update on Mission Viejo. She also attended the Newhart
Middle School Steam Building Dedication. She acknowledged that this was funded with primarily
Mission Viejo tax dollars. In 2006 an audit was conducted with Capistrano Unified School District
(CUSD) to find out where Mission Viejo tax dollars were being raised through 87-1 and Measure
A and our redevelopment money. We learned that the Mission Viejo taxpayers were paying more
but that the money was not going to our schools. This gave us an opportunity to meet with CUSD
to bring those tax dollars back to our schools. She encouraged residents to go and see the new Steam
Building at Newhart Middle School. Mayor Kelly announced that the Walk Against Drugs will be
held October 16 at 8:00 a.m. and the meeting point will be at the Murray Center. She discussed that
Senate Bills 760 and 761 which would be detrimental to Mission Viejo and to regional
transportation. Pointed out the co-op agreement between OCTA, San Clemente and the County
goes beyond legislation proposed by Senator Bates that appears to forever prevent an agency to
consider transportation improvements that traverse San Clemente by ignoring the need for
evaluation of all reasonable alternatives and ignoring San Clemente’s intentional efforts to block
transportation solutions. She stated that this affects Mission Viejo and outlined some of the co-op
agreement.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum voiced her opposition to the issue Mayor Kelley just discussed and she
is very disappointed in Supervisor Bartlett. She stressed that the City has accommodated our
neighbors with Alicia, Oso and Crown Valley Parkway and with the additional housing coming
this is more of an issue. She announced that she has an opening for the Investment Advisory
Commission and to apply with the City Clerk. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated that she went to
the League of California Cities Conference and met with a group that is preparing a collation
forming to put forth a Constitutional Amendment against SB9. She also visited a booth at the
league conference that establishes the “In God We Trust”. Asked residents to write a letter to
Congresswoman Katie Porter to ask why she didn’t’ advocate for our City to receive funding. He
thanked Cori Takkinen on her Legislative Report this evening.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 12, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  8  September 28, 2021
 ______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 12, 2021

City Council Minutes  9  September 28, 2021
